bib.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs". First author Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu (Yale), with Avi Caciularu, Gal Yona, Idan Szpektor (Google Research) and Arman Cohan (Yale). Venue: COLM 2026 (header "Published as a conference paper at COLM 2026"). arXiv:2606.32032v2, cs.CL, dated 12 Oct 2026; the 2606 prefix suggests v1 in June 2026. Code: github.com/yale-nlp/RLMF.
COVERAGE: 65 of 65 pages read, 222,022 chars. This includes appendices A–E, tables and prompts. I skimmed the reference list (pp. 11–24) and the long prompt, figure and example pages (pp. 29–35, 52–65) for content only.

The extraction was readable. No instructions were embedded in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Headline: RLMF beats standard GRPO ("RL", no metacognitive scaling) by up to 63% on numerical faithful calibration, measured as cMFG*. The 63% appears to be Qwen3-8B, 0.83 vs 0.51. Llama3.1-8B gives 0.84 vs 0.77.
 - Setup: SFT, then GRPO on 2000 PopQA samples, evaluated on 10 datasets at 1000 test examples each. Single training run per setting.
 - Quote: "outperforming standard RL by up to63%" (p.8). Table 1 (p.8) gives Qwen3-8B "+RL … 0.51 0.59 0.26" and "+RLMF … 0.83 0.57 0.19".
2. Against prior linguistic baselines (MetaFaith prompting, FUT SFT), the two-stage method gains 29% and 25% in average cMFG*.
 - Setup: the Table 1 average gains are quoted as 29% and 25%. In Table 1, Llama3.1-8B goes 0.60 base, 0.67 MetaFaith, 0.66 FUT, 0.82 RLMF+Rewrite.
 - Quote: "respective gains of29%and25%in average cMFG* across tasks" (p.8).
3. Small open models beat frontier models on faithful calibration, but not on accuracy. Both rows below are MetaFaith-prompted.
 - Gemini-3.1-Pro: cMFG* 0.70, Acc 0.78.
 - Qwen3-8B+RLMF: cMFG* 0.83, Acc 0.57.
 - Quote: "average gains of 37%, 17%, and 25% over GPT-5, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Gemini-3-Flash" (p.8).
4. Metacognitive data selection beats random and active-learning selection.
 - Setup: 2000 PopQA samples, chosen as the highest- and lowest-scoring halves of the model's own 0–100 self-rating.
 - Llama: cMFG* 0.84 vs 0.80 random vs 0.79 active learning.
 - Qwen3-8B: 0.83 vs 0.76 vs 0.72 (Table 3, p.9).
5. Generalisation: training on one dataset transfers.
 - Training on PopQA, SelfAware, HaluEval or UMWP gives average cMFG* 0.80–0.84 (Llama) and 0.81–0.83 (Qwen3-8B), against 0.60 and 0.54 for the untrained models (Table 2).
 - The UMWP-trained Llama has Acc 0.36 vs 0.41 for PopQA training (Table 26).
6. Human evaluation: win rate against FUT.
 - Setup: 3 expert annotators, 120 examples, Krippendorff's alpha 0.93.
 - Quote: "win rates of 98%, 98%, 95%, and 96% in dimensions of diversity, naturalness, helpfulness, and context suitability" (p.51).
7. Self-assessment improves: mean Zg rises during RLMF training (Fig. 25, D.3). The paper gives no number.
8. Sub-8B models follow the same pattern (Table 25).
 - Qwen3-4B: RL 0.76 vs RLMF 0.83.
 - Qwen3-1.7B: RL 0.75 vs RLMF 0.82.

HOW THE METACOGNITIVE REWARD IS BUILT (it is advantage scaling, not an extra reward)
- Each completion is a list of sentences with a confidence c_i. GRPO uses G=32 samples per prompt, with no std normalization: A_g = rho_g − mean(rho).
- Gold FC: F_gold = fraction of sentences with |c_i − g_i| < tau, where g_i is intrinsic confidence from sampling consistency (20 extra samples) and tau=0.10.
- F_pred: the policy is prompted online to output a score in [0,1] for how faithful its confidences are.
- Z_g = 1 − (F_pred − F_gold)^2.
- A_g is split into other rewards o_g and the faithfulness component f_g. A_RLMF = (o_g − mean o) + (f_g − mean f)·(k+Z_g) if f_g > mean f, else (f_g − mean f). k=1.
- Quote: "among completions that already perform well on the target task, we assign greater weight to those for which the model more accurately judges its own performance" (p.5).
- Composite reward weights (p.38): w_faith=12, w_strict=3, w_soft=3, w_factual_calib=1, w_acc=1.
  - r_faith = mean_i[1−(c_i−g_i)^2] (a Brier analog).
  - Factual calibration is a Brier term against accuracy. Accuracy is binary, judged by an LLM.
  - Format rewards: strict is ±1, soft is in [−1, 0].

BASELINES
- MetaFaith prompting and FUT SFT.
- Frontier models Gemini-3.1-Pro, Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-5, each with MetaFaith prompting.
- Standard RL, as the ablation.

ABLATIONS (all Llama3.1-8B, avg cMFG*)
- Z_g form (Table 12): quadratic 0.84, linear 0.77, square-root 0.74, 3/4-root 0.62.
- Z_g normalisation (Table 13): mean-centred 0.80, z-scored 0.71.
- Scaling scope (Table 14): scaling the entire advantage gives 0.71 and accuracy 0.17. Scaling the whole group gives 0.69.
- k (Table 16): k=1 gives 0.84. k=0 gives 0.69, k=2 gives 0.76, k=4 gives 0.71.
- tau (Table 17): 0.05 gives 0.74 vs 0.84 for 0.10.
- Z_g as an extra reward instead (Table 15): best variants reach about 0.79–0.83 but accuracy falls to 0.22–0.31. RLMF reaches 0.80 and 0.41 in the same setup. The authors report reward hacking without a faithfulness threshold, and say advantage scaling needs "far fewer hyperparameters".
- Pre-SFT (Table 11): Llama is +SFT 0.72 and +SFT+RLMF+MDS 0.84. Qwen3-8B without SFT, +RLMF only, is 0.70, and with SFT+RLMF+MDS it is 0.83. SFT is needed for the format.
- Data selection (Table 18): highest-and-lowest 0.77, highest only 0.75, lowest only 0.75, active-learning lowest 0.71.
- Reward leave-one-out (Table 6, preliminary, no SFT): removing a format reward gives cMFG* 0.48 or 0.55, vs 0.65 with all rewards. Removing the accuracy reward drops Acc to 0.27.
- Faithfulness reward form (Table 7): quadratic 0.65, linear 0.57.
- Training size (Table 10): 1000 → 0.80, 2000 → 0.84, 4000 → 0.80.

Notes bearing:
- Note 07 (reward design): the Brier-style faithfulness reward, weighted multi-reward sum, format rewards and the reward-hacking finding for an extra metacognitive reward.
- Note 08 (reasoning RL / GRPO variants): advantage shaping, and removing std normalization after Liu et al. 2025c (Dr. GRPO style).
- Note 03 (preference optimization): relation to RLHF and "RL with internal feedback". The paper says RLIF "initially improve training outcomes but can degrade performance", and claims RLMF avoids this.

LIMITS
- No limitations section. The ethics statement only urges caution about autonomous behaviour and says improved faithfulness is "not a substitute for verification".
- Only random seed 42 is stated. There are no error bars or multiple seeds, and the gaps rest on single runs.
- Checkpoints are selected on the in-domain test set (PopQA test, at most 1000 examples), which leaks a little into the headline numbers.
- Models are 1.7B–8B (Qwen3, Llama3.1-8B), using LoRA rank 64, with thinking mode off. Larger and reasoning models are untested. The authors speculate that tau=0.05 may behave differently for larger models.
- The task is faithful calibration only. The authors say variants "may depend on the specific target task", and they do not test RLMF on a general task such as math.
- Footnote 11: self-assessment gains are "not equivalent to broad metacognitive awareness".
- Standard RL on Qwen3-8B collapses (cMFG* 0.51, "gibberish" outputs), so the 63% partly reflects a weak baseline. Rewriting needs an extra LLM (Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite).
- Accuracy stays well below frontier models, for example 0.57 vs 0.78.
- Human evaluation compares only against FUT.
- cMFG* is a new metric the authors propose, and the baselines are scored on it.

BUILDS ON
- GRPO (Shao et al., 2024).
- Removing advantage normalization (Liu et al., 2025c).
- Confidence-scaled advantages: Seed-GRPO (Chen et al., 2025), and Zhang & Zuo 2025.
- Brier-style rewards: Damani et al., 2026, and Zhang et al., 2025b.
- RL with internal feedback (Zhang et al., 2025c;e).
- MetaFaith (Liu et al., 2025a), FUT (Eikema et al., 2025), and the cMFG metric (Yona et al., 2024).

CODE: no code snippets. The implementation is a modified trl GRPOTrainer advantage computation, in the linked repo.

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p.2), the pipeline overview. Fig. 2 (p.5), the RLMF flow from F_gold and F_pred to Z_g to scaled advantage. Fig. 3 (p.9), reliability diagrams where FUT fails at low confidence. Fig. 25, the Z_g trend during training. I did not run the figure script.

PROBLEMS: none beyond table-column garbling in the extraction. A few cells are run together, such as "0.800.41", so I read them against neighbouring rows.

QUOTES (verbatim)
- p.2: "we use the accuracy of the model's self-judgments to scale each completion's advantage, i.e., the relative learning signal that determines how strongly that completion is reinforced compared to alternative sampled completions."
- p.8: "outperforming standard RL by up to63%."
- p.44: "Without use of τfaith, models can exhibit a tendency toward reward hacking and FC performance is worsened."
